citeinfo.title: Compilation of surface water diversion sites and daily withdrawals in the Upper Colorado River and Little Colorado River Basins, 1980-2022
Database of surface water diversion sites and daily withdrawals for the Upper Colorado River Basin, 1980–2022

descript.abstract: This data release contains an inventory of 1,358 major surface water diversion structures with associated daily time series withdrawal records (1980-2022) for structures within the Upper Colorado River and Little Colorado River Basins. Diversion structures were included in this dataset if they were determined to have the capacity to divert water at rates greater than 10 cubic feet per second. Since those river basins encompasses portions of five states, water use data are dispersed among numerous federal and state agency databases and there is no centralized dataset that documents surface water use within the entire UCOL at a fine spatial and temporal resolution. Diversion structures and locations were identified from a mix of state reports, maps, and satellite imagery. A Python script was developed to automate retrieval of daily time series withdrawal records from multiple state and federal databases. The script was also used to process, filter, and harmonize the diversion records to remove outlier values and estimate missing data. The original withdrawal data, the processed datasets, and the Python script are included in this data release.
descript.purpose: This data release was compiled to provide a comprehensive data set of surface water diversion records for the Upper Colorado River and Little Colorado River Basins. Detailed spatial and temporal information on the diversion of surface water for use within, or removed from, those basins is crucial information that can be used in the development of hydrologic models and other water resource assessments. This product supports one such assessment - a coupled groundwater-surface-water hydrologic model currently in development by the USGS. This data release is also designed to be a stand-alone product to aid researchers in addressing questions related to water use within the Upper Colorado River and Little Colorado River basins.
descript.supplinf:
The compressed file archive “scripts.zip” contains the Python script (ucrb_diversions.py) developed to automate retrieval of daily time series withdrawal records, harmonize these records with other site records that were not available for automated online retrieval, and filter and process all data into a centralized, consistent format. The script utilizes the Master Table and historic time series withdrawal records contained in the “input.zip” archive. Docstrings in the script describe data retrieval and processing steps. A Python environment (“ucrb_diversions.yml”) designed to be compatible with the Python script is also included. The publication dates listed in the metadata for sources of time series withdrawal records represent the dates that withdrawal data were retrieved from those databases and used to create the data sets provided in this data release.
This database is subject to improvements, including the addition of sites, refinement of water use types, and the expansion of time series records. The database may be updated once every two to three years as resources permit.
The time-series diversion values that were manually transcribed from records obtained from the Central Utah Water Conservancy District, the New Mexico Office of the State Engineer, the Utah Division of Water Rights, and the Wyoming State Engineer’s Office represent the exact values in those records.

Specifically, we would like to acknowledge numerous personnel at the Utah Division of Water Rights, Central Utah Water Conservancy District, the New Mexico Office of the State Engineer, the Wyoming State Engineer’s Office, and the Wyoming Water Resources Data System for their assistance.

attracc.attraccr: A complete description of the techniques used to evaluate the accuracy and ensure the quality of the data included in this data release is provided in Lopez_2024. Briefly, coordinates associated with each diversion location were confirmed with satellite imagery and manually updated as needed to best represent the physical point of diversion. Filtering steps were applied to remove errors and potential outliers from time series data. A complete documentation of the filtering steps is included in Lopez_2024 and in the Python script provided in the data release. Though similar datasets do not exist for direct comparison, we utilized surface water diversion time series records to calculate a “natural flows” dataset for multiple USGS stream gages, which was then compared to a natural flows dataset published by the United States Bureau of Reclamation (USBR Natural Flows). Natural flows were calculated as the sum of observed streamflow at the target stream gage and upstream depletions (which were estimated by applying consumptive use factors to withdrawal records). Estimated natural flow values were between 88-124 percent of USBR natural flow values at all gages (average: 104 percent, standard deviation: 10 percent). Though there are uncertainties and assumptions in both natural flow datasets, the close comparison validates data compilation workflow and demonstrates that surface water use in the Upper Colorado River and Little Colorado River Basins can be represented with site-specific withdrawal records.

dataqual.logic: The data values were checked to ensure that they fell within the ranges expected for daily diversion amounts. The data were also checked for duplicate values (none were found).

procstep.procdesc: 1. A detailed description of the techniques used to compile the data sets included in this data release are provided in Lopez_2024, and those techniques are summarized in steps (2) through (7).

2. Used a combination of CDSS PODs, UTDWR, NMOSE, Purcell_2000, Tyrrell_Russell_2001, AZDWR, NWIS, USBR, NHD_V2, and satelite imagery to identify points of diversion within the Upper Colorado and Little Colorado River Basins with the ability to withdraw at rates greater than 10 cubic feet per second.

3. All points of diversion were verified with satellite imagery, NHD_V2, and maps obtained from UTDWR commissioner reports. Points of diversion were manually updated as needed to best represent the point at which water is withdrawn for the source water body (for example, a river, reservoir, etc.).
4. Used the script “ucrb_diversions.py” to automate retrieval of digitalized diversion time series withdrawal records from CDSS, UTDWR, WYSEO, NMOSE, NWIS, and USBR.

5. Obtained diversion time series withdrawal records that were not available for online retrieval through requests to the New Mexico Office of the State Engineer, the Central Utah Water Conservancy District, and the Wyoming Water Resources Data System. Additional time series withdrawal records that were unavailable for online retrieval were found in scanned copies of Utah commissioner reports (accessed through UTDWR), and these records were manually transcribed.
6. Used the script “ucrb_diversions.py” to harmonize retrieved digitalized diversion time series withdrawal records with manually transcribed diversion records.

7. Used the script “ucrb_diversions.py” to filter outliers from all diversion time series records and fill in missing records with estimated values as needed. Detailed information regarding filtering and filling steps can be found in Lopez_2024.
